messages:
sanjay: Pushing a canary for equinox-7b (int4) to the dedicated A10 pool. Seeing OOMs + a lot of mem fragmentation during middling traffic. Anyone seen this pattern with 7b int4s?
kevin: Can you paste the exact config and the node type?
sanjay: Running on 4xA10-24G, batch_size=16, max_new_tokens=1024, kv_prefetch=true. OOMs show RSS spikes ~26GB then eviction thrash.
maria: 26GB on A10-24 sounds like kv/cache blowout. What's the encoder/decoder length distribution?
sanjay: Mostly 512 prompt tokens, responses ~200-400 on repro. Repro with loadtest: `ab -n 50 -c 8` against the canary route.
kevin: Try dropping default max_new_tokens to 256 for canary and lower batch_size to 8. Also toggle kv_prefetch off; prefetch + large batches = fragmentation.
sanjay: quick test: switched to batch_size=8 and max_new_tokens=256 -> stable for 30m so far, no OOM. Will run longer.
jamie: We should also try the int8 quantization baseline — sometimes int4 kernels allocate awkward pinned buffers that fragment. Can you run a small quant compare?
maria: +1. Run a perf sweep: int4 vs int8 on same binary, measure peak RSS and 95th latency. If int8 solves frag, then we can consider fallback tier.
sanjay: kicking off two canaries: equinox-7b-int4-canary-1 (batch8/max256/kv_prefetch=false) and equinox-7b-int8-canary-1 (batch16/max512/kv_prefetch=true). Will post results.
ops-bot: deploy started: equinox-7b-int4-canary-1 -> pool-a10-4 (job id: dply-9832)
kevin: If int4 still fraggy, try adding `kv_trim_threshold: 0.3` and `cache_slot_reserve: 0.1` (small patch to runtime). Also set `prefetch_window: 64` instead of unlimited.
jamie: Also log /proc/pid/smaps before and after eviction to capture fragmentation pattern. If we see many small anon_vmas it's frag.
sanjay: Good call. I'll attach smaps on next failure. Also lowering default route max_new_tokens to 256 for equinox-7b until we confirm stable.
maria: For the eval side, we saw slight quality regression with int8 on one of our instruction evals (0.8% BLEU-ish drop). If int8 reduces OOMs we need a small eval run to quantify real impact.
kevin: Agree — run the eval set (1000 prompts) with cached prefixes so it's same workload. If quality delta <1%, we can prefer int8 for Dedicated.
sanjay: Results update: int4 canary crashed after ~45m during a 12-concurrency spike. Attached smaps showed many small anon mappings and >20% wasted reserved area. int8 canary stable and 95p latency slightly worse (~6%).
maria: So action items: 1) lower default max_new_tokens to 256 for equinox-7b routes (sanjay) 2) run larger quality eval on int8 vs int4 (jamie) 3) runtime patch to trim/compact kv and add pref window (kevin) 4) monitor for 24h before rollout (everyone).
sanjay: I'll open a PR for the default change and paste links. Also enabling auto-fallback policy: if int4 OOM > 0.5% for 1h then route to int8 variant.
ops-bot: deploy succeeded: equinox-7b-int8-canary-1 -> pool-a10-4 (job id: dply-9840)
kevin: Thx. If we still see fragmentation on int4 after runtime compaction, we should consider a small allocator change (hugepage-backed arenas). That will need eng-infra signoff.
jamie: Starting eval run now (1000 prompts) and capturing quality and token/latency diff. Will post in ~2h.
maria: tagging @eng-oncall for visibility. :eyes:
sanjay: Thanks team. Will post logs/PRs and smaps attachment if we hit another crash.
